p01.why: f(false) reaches the end of a function that returns a value during constant evaluation, and the evidence says all compilers reject that.

p02.why: Reaching the end of main returns 0.

p03.why: x is declared again in the outermost block of the body.

p04.why: Different parameter types and different cv- or ref-qualifiers make separate overloads, and each call picks the expected one.

p05.why: A void function returns normally at its end, and calls is 1.

p06.why: A nested block can declare the parameter name again; there is no main.

p07.why: f(true) returns 1 before the end, so constant evaluation succeeds; a warning is not an error here.

p08.why: A top-level const on a parameter is dropped, so both are one function defined twice.

p09.why: The program calls main; Clang and GCC give a pedantic diagnostic, which -pedantic-errors makes an error, and EDG rejects.

p11.why: The program takes the address of main; this is a pedantic error on Clang and GCC and an error on EDG.

p12.why: A long first parameter is an implementation-defined form; the specification does not record this case, and my guess is that EDG accepts while Clang and GCC reject.

p13.why: Declarations can use incomplete types, and a deleted definition is exempt.

p14.why: __func__ outside a function: Clang accepts with a warning, and GCC and EDG reject.

p15.why: GCC rejects main(int) under -pedantic-errors; the specification implies Clang and EDG accept.

p16.why: The parameter may end before or after mark runs, and the program accepts both orders.

p17.why: An unnamed parameter is valid, and pick returns 0.

p18.why: main in a namespace is an ordinary function that can be called, and the result is 0.

p19.why: __func__ in main holds the plain name main on the matrix.

p20.why: A definition needs a complete parameter type.

p21.why: Parameter names can differ between declarations and in overrides; the definition's names apply, giving 12 and 6.

p23.why: EDG accepts main(double); my reading is that Clang and GCC reject it.

p24.why: Only the definition's parameter name amount is visible in the body, so count is not declared.

p26.why: main must not be a template.

p28.why: argv[argc] is null, and argv[0] points to a string when argc is positive.

p29.why: Control can reach the end of f; the compilers warn with -Wreturn-type, and -Werror makes the warning an error.

p30.why: Several declarations and one definition are valid, and f returns 0.

p31.why: main in a namespace with C linkage: GCC 14 and Clang 18 accept, and GCC 16, Clang 22, and EDG reject.

p32.why: Each group of declarations adjusts to one function, and the checks give 4, 5, and 6.

p34.why: All compilers accept three parameters; I assume the third one receives a non-null pointer, which the specification does not state.

p35.why: a is named twice in one parameter list.

p37.why: The declarations differ only in return type.

p38.why: A typedef name of a function type cannot define a function.

p39.why: With argc 1, pick reaches its end without a return, which is undefined; I assume the sanitizer stops at the missing return, though the specification does not say.

p40.why: __func__ holds check on the matrix, 6 bytes with the null character.

p41.why: A global variable must not be named main.

p42.why: EDG accepts four parameters; the evidence implies Clang and GCC reject them.

p43.why: A function definition cannot be inside a function body.

p45.why: main's return type must be int written out, not deduced.
